issue_context.summary: OneNote desktop can clear its topmost state after maximize, focus, movement, or an Edge full-screen transition while PowerToys still displays the Always On Top border.
known_information: The issue is labeled reproducible and assigned.
A maintainer reproduced OneNote losing its topmost attribute while the pinned border remains.
Other topmost utilities behave similarly except DeskPins, suggesting OneNote actively changes z-order.
inferences: Always On Top tracks the window as pinned but misses or loses a race on the event where OneNote clears WS_EX_TOPMOST.
issue_context.analysis: Current Always On Top can reassert topmost on selected foreground/location events, but the report demonstrates a state divergence between the pinned property/border and actual z-order. A current event-sequence trace can identify the missed event without reporter-specific assets.
initial_investigation: AlwaysOnTop.cpp stores a pinned window property separately from WS_EX_TOPMOST and has logic to reapply topmost when selected WinEvents fire.
Issue 17134 is closed as a duplicate of this canonical issue.

proposed_fixes.title: Reconcile tracked Always On Top windows after applications clear topmost
proposed_fixes.root_cause: OneNote clears WS_EX_TOPMOST during window/full-screen transitions while PowerToys retains its pinned property; the subscribed event set or ordering does not reliably trigger reassertion afterward.
plan: Trace WinEvents, style changes, and z-order around the OneNote/Edge transition while comparing pinned property and WS_EX_TOPMOST.
Debounce and reassert topmost for tracked windows after the identified transition, avoiding loops when the user or app intentionally closes/minimizes.
Add an app-compat regression harness that simulates an external topmost clear while the window remains tracked.
verification: Repeat the OneNote move/maximize and Edge full-screen sequence for many cycles and verify actual z-order and border remain synchronized.

confidence.rationale: The state divergence and code model are clear, but the exact missed WinEvent/race still needs tracing.
